question: A typical example of early cave architecture is the Lomas Rishi cave in the Barabar Hills of ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lomas Rishi Cave** is a prominent example of early **rock-cut architecture** located in the **Barabar Hills** in the **Jehanabad district** of **Bihar**.
 
• It was constructed during the **Mauryan period** in the **3rd century BCE**, making it one of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in **India**.
 
• The cave is famous for its **ornamental facade**, which mimics contemporary **wooden architecture** of that era, specifically resembling the front of a thatched-roof hut.
 
• The entrance is decorated with a row of **elephants** in a semi-circular frieze, moving towards **Stupa** symbols, showcasing the early artistic mastery of the **Mauryan** artisans.
 
• This cave represents the formative stage of the **Chaitya arch** (horseshoe arch) that became a defining feature of later **Buddhist** cave temples.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bihar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barabar Caves Group**:

 
 
• The **Barabar Hill Caves** consist of four main caves: **Lomas Rishi**, **Sudama**, **Karan Chaupar**, and **Visva Zopri**.
 
• The **Sudama cave** is considered the earliest in the group, dedicated by **Emperor Ashoka** in the **12th year** of his reign (around **261 BCE**).
 
 
 
• **Ajivika Sect**:
 
 
• Most of these caves were primarily dedicated by the **Mauryan** emperors **Ashoka** and his grandson **Dasharatha** to the **Ajivikas**.
 
• The **Ajivika** was a major heterodox ascetic sect of ancient **India** that competed with **Buddhism** and **Jainism**.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Significance**:
 
 
• A characteristic feature of **Mauryan** caves is the **Mauryan polish**, which gives the interior granite surfaces a mirror-like finish.
 
• This technique reflects the advanced masonry skills developed during the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nagarjuni Caves**:

 
 
• Located about **2 km** from the **Barabar Hills**, the **Nagarjuni Hills** contain three more caves, including the **Gopi cave**.
 
• Inscriptions found here mention **Dasharatha Maurya**, the grandson of **Ashoka**, confirming the continued royal patronage of the region in the late **3rd century BCE**.
 
 
 
• **Internal Layout**:
 
 
• The **Lomas Rishi cave** consists of two rooms: a large rectangular **hall** (mandapa) and a smaller, circular **inner chamber** (shrine) with a hemispherical roof.
 
• This layout indicates that the cave was used as a **place of worship** and assembly for the **ascetics**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**:
 
 
• The architectural style of the **Lomas Rishi** facade directly influenced the later **Buddhist Chaitya halls** at sites such as **Ajanta**, **Karle**, and **Kanheri**.
